summary:
Andranik Berberyan was born on August 15, 1994 in
Yerevan, Armenia, in a family of musicians. From
2001 to 2008 he studied violin and piano at the
Sayat-Nova School of music in Yerevan.
In 2016, he received the Bachelor's degree in
Composition from the Yerevan State Conservatory
(YSC), having studied in the class of Aram Satyan.
The same year, he received the Bachelor's degree in
Symphonic and Opera Conducting, having studied in the class of Ruben
Asatryan.
In 2018, he received the Master's degree in Composition from the YSC. During
the studies, he composed symphonic and chamber compositions.
 
From 2013, he has worked with the "Sharm Holding" company, as a composer
and arranger. From 2017, he has cooperated with the Domino Production
company, as a composer. He also worked with numerous ensembles and
orchestras, such as the Armenian State Symphony Orchestra, the Armenian
Philharmonic Orchestra, "Harutyunyan" woodwind-piano quartet, the State Youth
Orchestra, etc.
 
In 2016, along with composers A. Hovhannisyan, R. Antonyan, and S. Umroyan,
he co-founded and became the President of the "QuarterTone" NGO, that is
aimed at developing and promoting contemporary music in Armenia.
 
In 2017, he founded and became the President/CEO of “Symbolium", a music
education startup incorporated in the USA.

Berberyan composed the scores to many films such as Alter Ego (2016) , Roots
(2016), The Line (2016), The Line 2: 25 Years Later (2017), Erken Kisher (2018), The Sun, Mountains and Love (2019),
Cilicia: The Land of Lions (2019), Songs of Solomon (2020), Dream of Kafka (2020) and Amerikatsi (2022).

In 2020, he founded and became the Director of “Berberyan Production House".
 
In 2019, he was nominated for 2019 "Anahit" National Film Awards in the "Best
Composer of the Year" category for the original score of "Erken Kisher" movie.
